title: observability: token-level KV cost/latency dashboard + alert tuning and logging improvements
author: Aisha Rao
description: Motivation: Our token-level KV cache telemetry has been spotty for multi-tenant workloads and alert thresholds were producing frequent false positives during traffic spikes. This PR consolidates token/KV cost and latency metrics, adds tracing hooks for KV hot keys, expands logging for cache miss amplification cases, and ships a Grafana dashboard with tuned alerts for both hosted and dedicated deployments. The goal is actionable SRE alerts (low false positive rate) and clear per-route cost/latency breakdowns for customers and internal oncall. Changes included: 1) Metrics: add per-route token_count, kv_hits, kv_misses, kv_evictions, kv_miss_latency_p50/p95/p99, and per-model token_cost_estimate metrics emitted with the existing metrics lib and annotated with route_id/model_id tags. 2) Tracing: instrument KV get/put hot codepaths with span attributes hot_key=true/false, cache_ttl, and shard_id to make contention visible in traces. 3) Logging: improve structured logs on eviction cascades (include recent-prefetch keys, route, model, sequence_length_bucket) and reduce log level for expected transient misses to DEBUG to cut noise. 4) Dashboards: new Grafana dashboard panels for token-level cost breakdown (per-route and per-model), KV hit-rate heatmap, miss latency histogram, and hot-key tracing links. 5) Alerts: tuned alert rules for kv_miss_rate and kv_miss_latency with dynamic thresholds per-route based on baseline percentiles and a cooldown window to avoid alert storms during deploys. 6) Tests/CIs: unit tests for metric tag propagation and an e2e smoke test that validates dashboard panels render for synthetic workloads. Related: ENG-4521 (observability epic), ENG-4680 (kv cache hardening), SUP-1198 (customer report of noisy kv alerts). Rollout plan: feature gated behind obs.feature_token_kv_dashboard flag; gradual rollout to staging then canaries, then 25% production traffic, with rollback via flag and automated playbook linked in the runbook. Checklist: - [x] Metrics emitted with expected tags - [x] Traces include KV attributes - [x] Logs structured and noise reduced - [x] Grafana dashboard added and exported - [x] Alert rules tuned and validated against historical data - [x] Feature flag and rollout plan included Commits summary: - Add token-level KV metrics and cost estimation (aisha/obs/token-metrics) - Instrument KV runtime with tracing attributes (aisha/obs/kv-tracing) - Enhance structured logs for eviction cascades (aisha/obs/logging) - Grafana dashboard JSON export + provisioning job (aisha/obs/grafana) - Alert rules and alerting playbook (aisha/obs/alerts) - Tests: unit + e2e smoke (aisha/obs/tests) CI: The PR ran the full pipeline: unit, integration, lint, and e2e-smoke. Initial e2e-smoke failed on missing test fixture; after the test harness fix (separate small commit) all pipelines passed. Load test (perf-canary) run in staging showed a 3% telemetry overhead at p50 and 6% at p99 for traces; added sampling for KV tracing to 10% for high-QPS routes. Files changed (high level): - src/serving/kv/metrics.go (emit new metrics, tag propagation) - src/serving/kv/tracing.go (span attrs, sampling controls) - src/platform/logging/eviction_logger.go (structured eviction logs) - infra/grafana/dashboards/token_kv_cost_latency.json (dashboard panels and links) - infra/alerts/token_kv_alerts.yaml (alert rules with dynamic thresholds) - pkg/featureflags/flags.go (feature flag) - tests/obs/token_kv_metrics_test.go (unit tests) - tests/obs/e2e_token_kv_smoke.sh (e2e smoke script) Review thread highlights: - Miguel: requested dynamic-threshold explanation in the alert rule comments and a runbook link for on-call — addressed by adding comments and playbook (commit 4). - Priya: asked to reduce trace sampling for high-QPS model shards; added sampling config and made it adjustable at runtime via flags (commit 5). - Jordan: requested dashboard panel that correlates token_cost_estimate with route throughput — added a correlation panel and note in dashboard description (commit 3). - Ops (Liam): asked for a migration plan to ensure minimal dashboard churn for customers using managed Grafana; added backward-compatible panel ids and a migration note. Merge: Squash merge into main after CI green and approvals. Post-merge actions: - Bump observability-migrations version and schedule a sync with managed Grafana team - Run the rollout via feature flag and monitor alerts for 48 hours - Update public docs with dashboard screenshots and alert guidance (docs ticket created)
